objective.statement: Make onboarding faster: new hires currently take two days to get a green build, and the cause of that delay is unknown.
objective.success_definition: A new hire can get a green build in measurably less than the current two days, and the reasons the process previously took two days are identified.

goals.statement: Determine why new hires currently take two days to get a green build.
acceptance: The causes of the current two-day time from new-hire start to green build are identified and documented.

goals.statement: Reduce the time it takes a new hire to get a green build below the current two days.
acceptance: A new hire can get a green build in measurably less than two days.

include: The process by which a new hire gets the project to a green build

assumptions.statement: "Onboarding" here refers to the process by which a new hire gets the project's build to a green (passing) state.
The current baseline is two days from new-hire start to a green build, as stated.
There is an existing build/onboarding process whose steps can be inspected and timed.

open_questions.question: What target time to a green build defines success (how much faster is "faster")? The task states no numeric target.
Should the work stop at diagnosing why a green build takes two days, or also implement the changes that make onboarding faster? The deliverable form is not stated.
Which repository/build system and which parts of the onboarding process are in scope to inspect and potentially change?
In what environment do new hires build (OS, hardware, network/VPN, local vs CI)?

verification.spec: Have a new hire (or a fresh environment simulating one) follow the onboarding process and record the elapsed time from start to a green build; compare against the two-day baseline.
verification.expected: Time to a green build is measurably less than two days.

verification.spec: Review the documented diagnosis of where the two days from new-hire start to green build are spent.
verification.expected: The causes of the current two-day time are identified and agreed to be accurate.

deliverables.description: Analysis identifying why new hires currently take two days to get a green build.

factors: Task is underspecified: no numeric target, no stated scope, and no stated deliverable form.
Changes to build or onboarding tooling could affect all developers, not just new hires.
Diagnosis may depend on environment factors (hardware, network, access provisioning) outside the codebase.
